repos.relevance: Anthropic's official Python SDK ('anthropic' on PyPI) — the flagship client library for the Claude API.
repos.policy: No issue-first or prior-approval gate for code. Docs changes are issue-only ('To suggest changes, open an issue'). Structural gate: most of the SDK is Stainless-generated; only src/anthropic/lib/, examples/, and tests/lib/ are fully hand-written — edits elsewhere may conflict with the next codegen push, and .stats.yml/.github/workflows/_version.py are generator- or release-please-owned (do not edit). CLAUDE.md: check line provenance via the Stainless-Generated-From commit trailer before editing; generator-owned behavior bugs belong upstream in the generator/spec. No PR template. AI policy: Explicitly AI-friendly, no prohibition. CLAUDE.md opens: 'Context for contributors (human or AI) on how this SDK is put together, plus the things reviews most often come back to.'

repos.relevance: Anthropic's official TypeScript/JavaScript SDK (@anthropic-ai/sdk on npm) — the flagship JS client for the Claude API.
repos.policy: No issue-first or prior-approval gate for code; docs changes are issue-only. Structural gate: SDK is mostly Stainless-generated; the generator never touches src/lib/ and examples/, edits elsewhere may hit merge conflicts on regeneration. CLAUDE.md is narrow (Node-only module isolation rules for bundler safety). No PR template. AI policy: No prohibition. Sibling repo policy is explicitly AI-tolerant (Python SDK CLAUDE.md addresses 'contributors (human or AI)'); this repo's CLAUDE.md is technical guidance only, with no restriction on AI-authored contributions.

repos.relevance: Hugging Face's core Rust tokenization library powering transformers — one of the most-used components in the HF ecosystem.
repos.policy: No prior-approval/assignment gate, but a strict quality bar: keep PRs as drafts until fully owned ('A PR marked ready for review is a claim that you have done the work'); bug fixes must include a regression test; fix the cause not the symptom; any performance claim requires before/after numbers from the tokbench benchmark on your machine with CPU/OS listed; byte-exactness of output ids is non-negotiable. No PR template or issue templates in .github. AI policy: Restriction, not prohibition. Exact text: 'No AI slop. Using a model to help is fine. Opening a PR you have not read, do not understand, and cannot defend is not.' Also: 'You are responsible for the code you push. If you cannot explain every line of your diff, why it is correct, and what it breaks if it is wrong — do not open it as ready for review.' AI-assisted work is explicitly permitted if the author can defend every line.

repos.relevance: Ai2's original flagship open language model training repo (OLMo 1/2 era), now superseded by OLMo-core.
repos.policy: CONTRIBUTING.md is a standard welcoming fork-and-PR guide (no approval gate, tests + CHANGELOG expected), but it is superseded in practice by the README deprecation notice; the repo has had no merges since 2025-11-24. AI policy: No AI/agent contribution policy found in CONTRIBUTING.md or README; no AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md/copilot files exist.

repos.relevance: The SWE-agent team's flagship minimal software-engineering agent (100-line agent used in SWE-bench research and as a reference implementation).
repos.policy: No approval gate. docs/contributing.md opens 'We happily accept contributions!' and points to good-first-issue/help-wanted labels. Style gates: minimalism is enforced ('This repository rewards minimal code'), pre-commit required, specific commit-message format (fix/feat/enh/docs/ref/chore with component). PR template is minimal (reference the issue). AI policy: No prohibition — the repo ships AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md/copilot-instructions.md specifically to guide AI contributors. It even acknowledges LM-written code and asks for cleanup: 'Many LMs write very verbose code -- please clean it up!' Only trailer rule: 'Do NOT add Co-authored-by: Cursor lines to the commit message.'

repos.relevance: Cline's flagship product — one of the most popular open-source AI coding agents / VS Code extensions (69k+ stars).
repos.policy: Issue-first with maintainer approval for features, with an explicit small-fix exception. CONTRIBUTING.md: 'All contributions must begin with a GitHub Issue, unless the change is for small bug fixes, typo corrections, minor wording improvements, or simple type fixes that don't change functionality.' Features require a Feature Requests discussion and 'Wait for approval from core maintainers before starting implementation.' 'PRs without approved issues may be closed.' PR template repeats the exception verbatim ('Limited exceptions: Small bug fixes, typo corrections, minor wording improvements, or simple type fixes... may be submitted directly without prior discussion.'). AI policy: No prohibition on AI-authored contributions found in CONTRIBUTING.md, AGENTS.md, copilot-instructions.md, or the PR template. The project is itself an AI coding agent and ships extensive in-repo agent instructions (AGENTS.md, .claude/, .agents/, .clinerules/). CONTRIBUTING.md closes: 'Contributing to Cline isn't just about writing code - it's about being part of a community that's shaping the future of AI-assisted development.'

repos.relevance: Nous Research's flagship open-source personal AI agent (Hermes), their primary public codebase and community focal point.
repos.maintenance: pushed 2026-09-24 — CAUTION: metrics anomalous (248k stars vs 960 watchers, 43k open issues; heavy bot activity)
repos.policy: No prior-approval gate; search-first is required (search open AND merged PRs/issues before building; 'For larger work, comment on the issue to signal you're working on it'). Hard scope exclusions regardless of quality: new memory providers under plugins/memory/ are closed ('We are no longer accepting new memory providers into this repo'), and any third-party product integration plugin must ship as a standalone plugin repo. AGENTS.md rubric rejects speculative infrastructure, new HERMES_* env vars for non-secret config, new core tools when a skill suffices, and cache-breaking changes. An automated triage sweeper closes PRs on implemented_on_main/cannot_reproduce/incoherent. PR template requires Conventional Commits, tests for bug fixes, duplicate search, platform tested. AI policy: Explicitly AI-welcoming, no prohibition. AGENTS.md opens: 'Instructions for AI coding assistants and developers working on the hermes-agent codebase.' Contribution priorities put bug fixes first; quality/premise-verification rules apply equally to human and AI authors.
